correctness.rationale: PASS. Cauchy projection formula for the solid cone gives B_k(z)=pi*z/2+(1/4) integral_0^{2pi}|k sqrt(1-z^2) cos(phi)+z|dphi and the axial branch pi*z. Setting x=z/(k sqrt(1-z^2))=sin(a) reduces the nonaxial branch to G_k(a)=k[cos a+(pi/2+a)sin a]/sqrt(1+k^2 sin^2 a). The derivative sign is D(a)-k^2 sin a cos a. H(a) has a unique minimum at tan(2a_s)=pi+2a_s, giving at most one nonaxial local maximum. The maximum of the G_k branch is strictly increasing from 0 to infinity and crosses pi exactly once, after H-minimum. The equality stationary equation D(a)[D(a)+cot a]=pi^2 singles out the transition. Independently solving it gave k_c=2.6414025520640956, |u_z|=0.5889810763491234 and saddle k_s=2.145539290889752; independent one-dimensional optimization checked k=1.5,k_c,3,5. The proof classifies all directions including axial/oblique ties, not merely stationarity.
